title: fix: isolate cache writes of pull request triggered reusable workflows
body:
## Checklist

### Compliance

- [x] I confirm that I make this contribution in accordance with [Forgejo's AI Agreement](https://codeberg.org/orbit/governance/src/commit/9084720dc6a7fbf1d3f358919d46bd6adfb55287/AIAgreement.md).

## Summary

A reusable workflow (`workflow_call`) triggered by a pull request can write cache
entries that later trusted runs restore. `getWriteIsolationKey` assigns the pull
request write isolation key only for the `pull_request` event name, but the server
rewrites the event name of reusable jobs to `workflow_call` for input evaluation
while retaining the original ref (`refs/pull/N/head`) and pull request payload in
the task context. A reusable job triggered by a pull request therefore falls
through to the empty (trusted) isolation key and can plant cache entries that
trusted runs (pushes to the default branch, manual dispatch) later restore.

## Affected versions

Confirmed on Forgejo 16.0.7 with Runner v12.13.2. The same check is unchanged in
Runner v13.2.1 and on current main, which this pull request targets.

## Reproduction

On our own instance, with a harmless marker payload and no credentials or real
data involved:

1. A workflow triggered on `pull_request` calls a reusable workflow that saves a
   unique marker under a fixed cache key.
2. A manually dispatched workflow in the same repository restores that key.
3. The trusted reader restored the marker written by the pull request. Expected:
   a cache miss.

## Fix

Treat a `workflow_call` job whose ref starts with `refs/pull/` like the
`pull_request` event that triggered it, so its cache writes stay isolated to that
pull request's runs. Jobs triggered by pushes or manual dispatch keep the trusted
namespace, and the existing merged/closed pull request semantics are preserved.

The condition is precise: only pull request head refs use the `refs/pull/`
prefix; branch refs are `refs/heads/...` and tag refs are `refs/tags/...`, so no
other event type is affected.

## Tests

`TestRunner_getWriteIsolationKey` gains subtests for `workflow_call` from an open
pull request, a closed and not merged pull request, a closed and merged pull
request, and from a push.

## Verification

- `go test ./... -args -features "-"` passes.
- The live reproduction above was re-run against the patched runner on our
  instance: the trusted reader now misses the marker.

## Disclosure

This issue was reported privately to the Forgejo security team on 2026-11-09, and
the security team supports addressing it through public review. AI tools assisted
with the analysis and the drafting of this change; the author is accountable for
it.

title: fix: host-mode docker default network
body:
Fixes #1789

Fall back to Docker network mode "default" for Docker job steps in host-mode Forgejo runner.

Currently, in host mode and with no manual `container.network` configuration, docker:// job steps use the "WORKFLOW-xxx" job network, which is not created/initialized in host mode and thus starting the container fails (see #1789). Container and Dockerfile actions work because they use Docker's "default" network in [act/runner/action.go#L499-L502](https://code.forgejo.org/orbit/orbit/src/tag/v13.2.1/act/runner/action.go#L499-L502). This PR uses the same logic as there: if `rc.JobContainer.ManagesOwnNetworking()` is set and there is no `container.network` configured, use the "default" network.

Claude code helped me find the source of the problem; I wrote the fix and tests (mostly copy-pasted from the test case above in the same file) myself.

title: fix: use printf in the default shell probe so macOS /bin/sh works
body:
The default-shell probe for non-host backends uses echo -n bash. On macOS, /bin/sh is bash 3.2 in POSIX mode, which prints -n bash\n

printf is POSIX and unambiguous. Probe output tested with dash (Debian, Ubuntu), bash (Fedora), BusyBox ash (Alpine, BusyBox; falls back to sh) and macOS: unchanged everywhere except macOS, where it's now correct.

title: fix: don't panic when a cancelled job runs composite post steps
body:
Post steps of a cancelled job run on a fresh context with no job error container, so SetJobError panics and kills the runner process along with every other job it is running.
